solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Struck by church turning sophisticated

parts.note: struck, as in hit a ball

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the abbreviation for church is read backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone is dazzled by a church that has gone upmarket and modern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the struck word beside the turned church.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tec is a variant of hi-tech, describing advanced, technically sophisticated equipment or design.

clue.text: Tropical bird with hard, round bill that was unknown at home

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
a round letter
a parliamentary bill, once passed, becomes an act
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A tropical bird is described with a hard round beak that had gone unrecorded in its native land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a beak, but 'bill that was' is a law already passed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoatzin is a South American bird of swampy forests; hoactzin is an older spelling of its name.

clue.text: Death of military alliance, seconds after which base abandoned

indicators.note: in a down entry the base of a word is its bottom letter, and abandoning it drops that letter
after puts the alliance and the seconds behind the trimmed word in the build

parts.note: which and that are interchangeable relative pronouns
the North Atlantic Treaty Organization
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A grim report on the death of an alliance, its base deserted moments later.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer a word's base is its last letter, so the base of which's synonym is dropped before the alliance and seconds follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanatos is the Greek personification of death, and in Freudian theory the death instinct.

clue.text: Dictionary happening to contain note in post for steward

indicators.note: to contain means the joined dictionary and happening hold the next letters inside them

parts.note: Chambers is the dictionary used for barred crosswords like this
happening in the sense of fashionable
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry turns into a musical note within a posting for a steward.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted letters go between the dictionary's name and the happening word, not at the very middle. Chambers is the standard dictionary for these puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamberlain manages a royal or noble household, and the suffix -ship names the office he holds.

clue.text: In times long ago, recalled Cockney singer gaping

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; gaping is read as a verbal noun

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign

indicators.note: In at the front says the singer goes inside the letters that follow
recalled read as called back, so the phrase for long ago runs in reverse

parts.note: as in days of yore
Chas of the London duo Chas and Dave, known for Cockney singalongs

explanation.surface: A Cockney singer is remembered from times past, mouth wide open in song.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas and Dave were a London pub-rock duo famous for 'rockney' singalongs; 'gaping' is a botanical term here.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerochasy is a botanical term for seed vessels splitting open when they dry, a kind of gaping.

clue.text: Test, cycling up to find seabirds

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word for test runs backwards
cycling moves letters round from one end to the other like a wheel turning

parts.note: an exam is a test

explanation.surface: An examination of a cycling route uphill to look for seabirds.
explanation.walkthrough: EXAM upwards is MAXE; moving MA from the front to the back gives XEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Xema is the genus name of the fork-tailed Sabine's gull, so the word stands for those gulls.

clue.text: Walter's charming fellow miner Karen's crazy for

indicators.note: crazy implies disorder, so the miner and Karen are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Karen is mad about a charming miner called Walter.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter is Sir Walter Scott, who used this word; the apostrophe on Walter makes it his.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott used reimkennar for a person with magical powers, one who can enchant or charm through verse.

clue.text: Shy woman left behind absorbing legal documents and flyer

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the woman left behind holds the documents

parts.note: to shy is to throw
a woman whose husband has died
wills are legal documents left at death

explanation.surface: A timid widow reads through her late husband's will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid, but it is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: The chuck-will's-widow is a North American nightjar named after its call, so it is a bird that flies.

clue.text: European magistrate's time in ME capital

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the name of the city

parts.note: Amman is the capital of Jordan in the Middle East (ME)
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A European official spends some time in a Middle Eastern capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ME looks like Maine or the pronoun, but here it is the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: An amtman is a district bailiff or administrator in Germany, Scandinavia and the Netherlands, a local judicial officer.

clue.text: After year book, torn and no longer used, incinerated

indicators.note: After sets the torn piece behind the abbreviations for year and book

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year
B is the abbreviation for book
rent as the past tense of rend, to tear

explanation.surface: After a year, an old book was torn up and burned.
explanation.definitionFit: Ybrent is an obsolete Spenserian past participle of burn, so an archaic word for burnt.

clue.text: Belligerent cries from attention seeker getting in the way of large meeting earlier

indicators.note: earlier places the meeting part ahead of the call that grabs attention

parts.note: à la means in the manner of
L is the abbreviation for large
an annual general meeting
oi! is a shout to get someone's attention

explanation.surface: A noisy heckler blocks the path of a big meeting held before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' joins the call to the rest, and 'earlier' says the rest comes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alalagmoi are ancient Greek battle shouts, war cries raised before charging the enemy.

clue.text: Quote theory that's been oddly overlooked, say

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are ignored, leaving only the even ones

parts.note: letters two, four, six, eight and ten

explanation.surface: Someone quotes a theory that has strangely been ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to speak it aloud, a straightforward synonym for the verb say.

clue.text: Tango: dance seen in Tibetan balls?

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Brazilian dance

explanation.surface: A tango is a dance you might see at a ball in Tibet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balls' suggests dances, but the definition means food rolled into balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsamba is roasted barley flour, a Tibetan staple often kneaded with tea and butter into small balls.

clue.text: Home-brew passes around group of drinkers in the family

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for passes is read backwards

parts.note: gives the OK to; approves

indicators.note: in puts the drinkers inside the family

parts.note: one's kin is one's family
Alcoholics Anonymous, a group of former drinkers

explanation.surface: Home-brew gets handed round a drinking circle within the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes' looks like a verb about handing drinks round, but it is a plural noun of approvals.
explanation.definitionFit: Skokiaan is a potent illicit liquor brewed at home in southern Africa, an example of home-brew.

clue.text: Tip on training one football team's ability to tighten things up

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means sitting above, so the tip comes first

parts.note: a tip is a filthy place, like a pigsty
physical training
Roman numeral one
many English clubs are called City, such as Manchester City

explanation.surface: Advice on training gives a football team the ability to tighten up its defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' reads as advice, but in British slang a tip is a messy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Stypticity is the astringent quality of contracting body tissue, as a styptic does to stop bleeding.

clue.text: Drug, one drunk, dealing with onset of tetanus in one breaking leg

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: Roman numeral one
a sot is a drunkard
re means concerning

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so only its first letter counts

parts.note: first letter
taken as written
the on side in cricket is also called leg
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drunk with tetanus breaks a leg and needs drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, a convention setters lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotretinoin is a retinoid medication prescribed chiefly to treat severe acne.

clue.text: Savage, maybe cross at heart with expert using long words so?

parts.note: a pro is an expert

indicators.note: at the heart of something is in its middle, so the cross sits inside

parts.note: Lily Savage was the drag persona of British comedian Paul O'Grady
x is a cross

explanation.surface: An angry, savage critic sides with an expert who uses long words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savage' looks like an adjective, but it is the surname of a British drag act; 'maybe' marks Lily as one Savage.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolix means tediously wordy, so speaking prolixly is speaking at great length with many words.

clue.text: Spartan meal, never filling, scarcely satisfies: inept idea!

indicators.note: with no filling, each word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Spartan meal that never fills you and barely satisfies seems a poor idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan' suggests merely frugal, but here it means from ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: Syssitia were the communal messes where Spartan citizens ate together, so the term names their shared meal.

clue.text: Content of alpha rays dispersing across power line

indicators.note: dispersing scatters things, so these letters are spread out and rearranged
the scattering stretches across the following two items too, bringing them into the mix

parts.note: taken as written
P is the symbol for power
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A physics paper on what alpha rays contain as they spread across a power line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like a noun meaning contents, but it is the adjective meaning pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy as Larry is a British and Australian idiom for being very pleased and satisfied.

clue.text: Cease taking public transport, not to walk around Glasgow

indicators.note: not means leave out the word to that follows
taking in, so the word for cease holds the transport inside

parts.note: to cease is to stop
a tram is a form of public transport
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: Someone gives up the tram and decides to walk around Glasgow instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around Glasgow' belongs to the definition, marking a Scots word, rather than signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Stramp is a Scots verb meaning to tread or trample, a heavy kind of walking.

clue.text: Once used to talk over one's friend at first, rudely interrupting

parts.note: one is becomes I am, shortened

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking in, so the letter goes inside the friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: In the past, someone talked over a friend, rudely interrupting him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once used' says the word is obsolete; 'at first' governs rudely, giving R, which goes inside PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Imparl is an obsolete verb meaning to parley or confer, discussing terms with another party.

clue.text: Short break in a type of film showing an anteater

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to break in a horse is to tame it
taken as written
film noir, the dark crime genre

explanation.surface: A brief interval during a screening of a noir film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a pause, but 'break in' is the horse-training verb tame.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamanoir is another name for the giant anteater of Central and South America.

clue.text: Dreams of Scottish women's charity chasing pennies no longer

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the pennies come before the women and charity

parts.note: d was the symbol for the old pre-decimal British penny
W is the abbreviation for women
alms are charitable gifts

explanation.surface: Scotswomen dream of a charity that no longer needs to chase pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Scottish' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwalm is Scots for a swoon or daydream, so dwalms are Scottish dreams.

clue.text: Job following this native from Tartu via Lahti?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the abbreviation for the Old Testament book that comes just before the Book of Job
second meaning: an old word for an Estonian; Tartu is an Estonian city, Lahti a Finnish one, both Finnic peoples

explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' is the Bible book, not work. The question mark admits the native is of Finnic stock, hence the Finnish route.
explanation.definitionFit: Esth is short for Esther, the book before Job, and an archaic name for a person from Estonia.

clue.text: Flooded out after cutting pipe down

indicators.note: after being cut, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: someone out is away
sh! means be quiet

explanation.surface: A burst pipe has flooded the place after someone cut into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipe down' looks like a plumbing job but is the order to be quiet; AWAY cut becomes AWA.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means covered or overflowing with water, as a place that has been flooded.

clue.text: Saw centre from Kuwaiti XI despicably pulled back

indicators.note: pulled back means drawn backwards, so the letters read right to left
the answer is taken from the middle of the run of words

parts.note: the letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A Kuwaiti cricket eleven behaved badly and was withdrawn from the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the verb or tool, but here it is a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipse dixit, Latin for he himself said it, is a dogmatic assertion resting on authority, a saying like a saw.

clue.text: Folding altarpiece cloth, twice partially at the edges wrinkled

indicators.note: something wrinkled is crumpled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the outside letters of the preceding word are kept, here taken twice

parts.note: first and last letters
twice asks for a second copy of those same edge letters

explanation.surface: An altarpiece cloth that has been folded, creased at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' means the edge letters of partially, PY, go in two times.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyptych is an altarpiece made of several hinged panels that fold, beyond a triptych's three.

clue.text: Weaver attaching arrangement of hair on to which end?

indicators.note: on to means fixed after, so the hairstyle comes behind the question word

parts.note: to what end? means for what reason
a DA, short for duck's arse, is a 1950s quiff hairstyle

explanation.surface: A weaver puzzles over which end of the hair to attach to the loom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaver' suggests a craftsman, but it is a weaverbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The whydah or whyda is an African widowbird of the weaverbird family, so it is a weaver.
